_purpose: Declared supplements to the nightly preflight sweep's DERIVED stage list. The stage list itself is derived from infrastructure/step_function.json by infrastructure/preflight_sweep_stages.py and is never enumerated here. This file holds only the two things derivation cannot supply on its own — an acknowledgement for each stage that has NO dry path, and a value for each Map-scoped binding that exists only per-iteration at execution time. Both are checked for exact agreement with the definition by tests/test_preflight_sweep_stages.py, so a stage added to the pipeline fails CI at merge time rather than quietly shrinking the sweep's denominator.

no_dry_path_stages.reason: RATIFIED (alpha-engine-config#7329). Runs the model-zoo spec RESOLVER on the launcher box itself — a pure read of the zoo spec registry that launches no spot, spends nothing and writes nothing. It threads no $.preflight_args because there is no expensive path to short-circuit: the stage IS its own preflight. Its command is a raw `python -m training.model_zoo` invocation, not a `bash infrastructure/*.sh` script, so it cannot be threaded into the sweep's launcher-detection contract (infrastructure/preflight_sweep_stages.py's `_LAUNCHER_RE`) without a `bash infrastructure/*.sh`-shaped wrapper in crucible-predictor — out of scope for this stage's own risk. COMPENSATING SURFACES, named concretely: (1) a substrate defect that would break it (missing repo, broken venv, unreadable spec file) breaks the sweep-covered PredictorTraining and ModelZooSelect stages first — both SWEEPABLE and exercised every sweep run; (2) ANY resolve/parse failure in this stage (a real exception, not just an empty list) is caught and converges on the `PublishModelZooFailureImmediate` SNS-publish state (step_function.json — 'the SOLE convergence point for all five model-zoo rotation fail-open Catches', alpha-engine-config#6722), which pages on every live run regardless of the sweep, and also sets the `$.model_zoo_degraded` flag the completion notifier reads.

RATIFIED (alpha-engine-config#7329). Post-workload observability producer (health_checker.py --alert) on the launcher box. It is a CONSUMER of the run's outputs, not a precondition of them — running it dry before the run would assert nothing about whether the run can start. Beyond the consumer/precondition argument: step_function.json's own Comment on this state records a DELIBERATE prior architecture decision (config#902's shell-run comment) that this stage 'has no skip gate by design and runs for-real (not dry) even under shell_run' because health_checker.py implements no --preflight-only flag to receive $.preflight_args — giving it a dry path now would reverse that ruled decision, not merely fill a gap. COMPENSATING SURFACE for the boot-failure gap sf-pipeline-policy §9.2a raises (a checker that cannot start reporting nothing, read as nothing-to-see): this stage's `Catch: States.ALL` (step_function.json) fires on EVERY failure mode including a boot/import failure on the box, routes to `SaturdayHealthCheckDegraded`, sets `$.health_check_degraded`, and that flag is read by `CheckGateDegradedNotify`/the completion notifier on every live Saturday run — a checker that cannot boot produces a visible DEGRADED completion email, not silence.

RATIFIED (alpha-engine-config#7329). Post-workload substrate/artifact assertion on the launcher box (crucible-dashboard's infrastructure/substrate_health_check.sh), same consumer-not-precondition argument as SaturdayHealthCheck. Its own dry path would be a no-op: it grades artifacts that only exist after the stages ran. step_function.json's Comment on this state records the same DELIBERATE config#902 decision as SaturdayHealthCheck — 'Deliberately does NOT thread $.preflight_args ... this pair has no skip gate by design and runs for-real even under shell_run, and substrate_health_check.sh has no --preflight-only flag to receive it' — so adding one here reverses a ruled decision rather than filling an oversight. COMPENSATING SURFACES, concretely: (1) this stage's `Catch: States.ALL` routes any boot/infra failure to `SubstrateHealthCheckDegraded`, sets `$.health_check_degraded`, and that reaches `CheckGateDegradedNotify` on every live run, same as SaturdayHealthCheck; (2) per-row validation failures (as opposed to the checker's own boot failure) are independently covered — the stage's own Comment: 'Per-row CloudWatch metrics emit to AlphaEngine/Substrate so individual rows have their own alarms', which fire regardless of whether this SF stage's own boot succeeded.

alpha-engine-config-I7267. Runs a single `aws s3api head-object` on the same instance, dispatched ONLY when PitParityLookahead already exited non-zero (checks for the RESOURCE_KILL marker key PitParityLookahead's own commands write). It threads no $.preflight_args and has no dry variant: there is no expensive path to short-circuit — the check IS a single, ~sub-second, already-cheap S3 API call, and running it against a marker key that (on a dry/--preflight-only day) never gets written simply resolves to 'not found', which is the correct, harmless outcome, not a defect to guard against. COMPENSATING SURFACES: (1) a substrate defect that would break this trivial head-object call (broken IAM, unreachable S3, instance gone) would first and more visibly break PitParityLookahead's own artifact PUT two steps earlier, which routes to the existing PitParityLookaheadDegraded fail-open and pages via $.parity_degraded; (2) this check's own Catch (send/poll failure) already falls back to that SAME PitParityLookaheadDegraded terminal — it can only ADD the RESOURCE_KILL classification on top of an already-covered degrade, never introduce a new uncovered failure mode.
alpha-engine-config-I7267. Same shape and argument as PitParityLookaheadResourceKillCheck, for the walkforward pass's RESOURCE_KILL marker key.

_dedicated_box_purpose: DECLARED stages that are DERIVED-UNSWEEPABLE because the stage does not run on the sweep's own box. A stage listed here threads $.preflight_args and is preflight-capable, but its launcher and venv live on a DEDICATED box that the stage's own dispatcher bootstraps at run time — so the sweep's LAUNCHER box, which is the only box the sweep has, structurally cannot exercise it, however healthy everything is. That is a bounded, reviewed boundary of the denominator, not a coverage defect: the entry gives it its own unsweepable kind (`dedicated_box`), keeps it out of stages_unsweepable_coverage_defect and out of the persistent-unsweepable streak, and NAMES it on every surface — a non-blocking `dedicated_box` coverage finding, a row in results[] carrying the acknowledgement text, and the acknowledged-gaps block of the notification. An acknowledgement is never a silent exclusion, and it is graded BOTH WAYS by tests/test_preflight_sweep_stages.py and by manifest_disagreement() at run time: a stage acknowledged here that is no longer UNSWEEPABLE (it became sweepable, lost its dry path, or was removed) is a stale-entry finding, and an UNSWEEPABLE stage that is NOT acknowledged here keeps today's behaviour — coverage_defect, and the run fails.

dedicated_box_stages.reason: alpha-engine-config-I9329. EvalJudgeProcess runs the LLM-judge pass over an eval batch (crucible-research evals/judge_spot_run.py). nousergon-data-PR1593 (2026-08-29) moved it off the shared launcher box onto a DEDICATED spot box that the eval-judge-spot-dispatcher Lambda bootstraps itself: the dispatcher clones crucible-research to /home/ec2-user/crucible-research and builds its .venv there, and the SF command is `cd /home/ec2-user/crucible-research` + `/home/ec2-user/crucible-research/.venv/bin/python -m evals.judge_spot_run ... {$.preflight_args}`. WHY THE SWEEP CANNOT EXERCISE IT: the sweep runs on the LAUNCHER box (built by the weekly launcher bootstrap, checkout_root /home/ec2-user), which carries the same repo under the name `alpha-engine-research` and has no crucible-research/.venv at all — so the derivation resolves the stage's launcher to /home/ec2-user/crucible-research/evals/judge_spot_run.py, finds no such file, and classifies it UNSWEEPABLE with reason 'launcher not present in the checkout'. The file DOES exist on crucible-research main and DOES implement --preflight-only; nothing is broken, and no arrangement of the launcher box makes this stage measurable, because the box the stage runs on does not exist until its dispatcher creates it. Observed as stages_unsweepable_coverage_defect=1 - the SOLE failure input - on every nightly run from 2026-08-30 to 2026-09-06 (7 consecutive runs against a streak threshold of 8, i.e. one run short of also escalating as a persistent_unsweepable finding). COMPENSATING SURFACES, named concretely: (1) evals.judge_coverage.enforce_coverage RAISES on any plan/graded gap, so a judge pass that silently covered less than its plan cannot complete; (2) judge_spot_run exits 3 on its own precondition failures, which fails the SSM command and therefore the STAGE - the failure the sweep would have pre-empted still surfaces loudly on the live run rather than being swallowed; (3) the stage's Catch converges on MarkEvalJudgeDegraded, which sets the degraded flag the completion notifier reads and pages; (4) the dispatcher's own watchdog and the spot-orphan reaper backstop the box itself, so a box that comes up and never finishes is not silent either. SOTA, and NOT what this entry is: the sweep should dispatch the dedicated box itself in --preflight-only mode rather than acknowledging that it cannot reach it, which would restore real coverage instead of declaring its absence. That is the tracked follow-up, alpha-engine-config-I10083; this acknowledgement is the honest interim state and is graded both ways so it cannot outlive its cause silently.

_upstream_purpose: DECLARED same-day upstream artifact dependencies. A stage listed here reads an artifact that a PRECEDING stage of the same execution produces, so its preflight cannot pass on a day the real pipeline has not already run — a --preflight-only run by definition does not produce its stage's output. Such a stage is UNSWEEPABLE that day (could not measure), never FAILED (found a defect). The classification is DECLARED HERE and nowhere else: it is never inferred from the launcher's stderr text, so rewording an error message cannot reclassify a real failure as unsweepable, and adding a dependency is a reviewed diff. Each declaration also states how its probe date is derived (see _date_normalization_reason) — the sweep probes the date the STAGE used, not its own calendar date. The declaration only ARMS the reclassification — the sweep still probes the named prefix on the day, and a stage that fails while its upstream prefix IS populated stays FAILED. Each declaration ALSO carries max_age_days (alpha-engine-config-I10717 (2)): before settling for 'unsweepable that day', the sweep walks backward from today, day by day, for the most recent date whose upstream prefix holds real content, and — if one exists within max_age_days — RE-DERIVES and RE-RUNS this SAME stage's own --preflight-only command against that override run_date (both spot_predictor_backtest.sh and spot_portfolio_optimizer_backtest.sh accept --run-date natively; the override only ever reaches the boot+deps+smoke path, since --preflight-only still gates everything past it). That turns the ~6-non-Saturday-nights-a-week case from unmeasured into a REAL pass/fail — a stage whose environment is broken now fails for real and pages, exactly like any other sweepable stage, instead of the breakage hiding behind 'awaiting upstream' until the next Saturday. Only when NO populated instance exists anywhere in the window does the stage stay upstream_pending/degraded — that is now a genuine staleness finding, not the ordinary weekday state.
_unsweepable_streak_threshold_reason: A stage that is unsweepable on EVERY run for this many consecutive days is its own finding (the sweep covers nothing there), emitted separately from coverage_findings so it never reads as coverage. 8 days is one full weekly-pipeline cycle plus one: even with the max_age_days remeasurement (see _upstream_purpose), a stage can still be genuinely unsweepable for a whole week if the upstream has not been written in over max_age_days days, so a threshold of 7 or less would fire on a single slow week, and a threshold of 8 fires only when a whole weekly cycle passed without the stage ever becoming measurable — which means either the weekly pipeline stopped running or the dependency declaration is wrong. Counted in RUNS internally, derived as threshold_days x (1440 / cadence_minutes) from preflight_sweep_cadence.json, so changing the sweep cadence does not silently change what this means.

upstream_artifact_dependencies.reason: spot_predictor_backtest.sh's stage preflight asserts spot_common_s3_prefix_nonempty "backtest/${RUN_DATE}/" — the Backtester stage's sweep output. Backtester's own --preflight-only run exits before producing it, so on any day the real weekly pipeline has not run, this stage's preconditions are unknowable rather than broken. Reported as FAILED on the sweep's first run (preflight-sweep-20260814T080010Z), which is alpha-engine-config#7323. max_age_days=8 (one full weekly cycle plus one day of slack, same rationale as unsweepable_streak_threshold_days): the sweep re-derives and re-runs this stage's own --preflight-only command against the most recent populated backtest/{date}/ within that window (spot_predictor_backtest.sh accepts --run-date natively), so the stage is MEASURED for real on every non-Saturday night, not merely acknowledged as unmeasurable — alpha-engine-config-I10717 (2).

spot_portfolio_optimizer_backtest.sh asserts the same prefix, one link further down the Backtester -> PredictorBacktest -> PortfolioOptimizerBacktest chain. Same structural argument, same first-run false failure. Same max_age_days=8 remeasurement rationale as PredictorBacktest — alpha-engine-config-I10717 (2).

_date_normalization_reason: NON-INFERABLE GOTCHA, measured 2026-08-26. The sweep binds run_date to its own UTC CALENDAR date, exactly as the SF's InitializeInput does — but no backtester stage reads that value directly: spot_predictor_backtest.sh and spot_portfolio_optimizer_backtest.sh both call spot_common_normalize_run_date (crucible-backtester infrastructure/_spot_common.sh), which snaps RUN_DATE back to the NYSE trading day BEFORE the stage preflight reads backtest/${RUN_DATE}/. On every Saturday, Sunday and market holiday the stage and the sweep therefore name DIFFERENT prefixes, and the safety property stated in _upstream_purpose — a stage that fails while its upstream prefix IS populated stays FAILED — is void: the sweep probes the always-empty calendar-dated prefix and downgrades a REAL failure to upstream_pending, which does not page. Observed on 2026-08-22 and 2026-08-23, where both stages PASSED against the populated backtest/2026-08-21/ while the sweep's own probe would have named an empty backtest/2026-08-22|23/. Declared here rather than inferred: the sweep applies this normalization to the probe date only, through the same nousergon_lib.trading_calendar chokepoint the launcher uses, and reports the stage UNMEASURED rather than falling back to the calendar date when that library is unavailable. Closed vocabulary: none | nyse_trading_day.
_ignore_subprefixes_reason: NON-INFERABLE GOTCHA. s3://alpha-engine-research/backtest/<date>/ EXISTS on a day nothing produced it, because the sweep's OWN phase markers (.phases/preflight.json, .phases/runtime_smoke.json) are written under it. A probe testing prefix EXISTENCE rather than prefix CONTENT would read as satisfied and measure nothing — it would silently re-classify every real upstream failure as a genuine stage failure and every genuine failure as real, i.e. it would do nothing at all while appearing to work. Keys under an ignored sub-prefix, and zero-byte keys, do not count as upstream content.

spec_id.reason: ResearchPredictorParallel.ModelZooTrainMap.TrainSpecDispatch is Map-scoped: $.spec_id is supplied per iteration from the resolved zoo spec array and has no value outside an execution. The sweep exercises the stage's BOOTSTRAP-CLASS preconditions (clone, venv, lib pin, imports, dispatcher-side file checks), all of which spot_train_spec_dispatch.sh asserts before the spec id is ever read — its --preflight-only path exits 0 ahead of any spec-dependent work, so the value is a placeholder and never selects real work. If that ordering ever changes, the stage's preflight would fail loudly against a spec that does not exist, which is the correct outcome and not a silent pass.

eval_judge_submit.reason: alpha-engine-config-I9329. EvalJudgeProcess's command reads $.eval_judge_submit.Payload.{batch_id,plan_s3_key}, which EvalJudgeSubmit* returns at RUN TIME — there is no execution input for the sweep to derive them from, so they are declared here for the same reason spec_id is. Both are placeholders and neither can select real work: evals/judge_spot_run.py returns 0 from its --preflight-only block BEFORE either value is read (the block runs the imports and one read-only list_objects_v2 against the bucket, then returns), and the sweep threads $.preflight_args exactly as every other sendCommand stage does. Nested rather than flat because sf_commands._resolve walks the dotted path through the binding, so a flat string would raise UnresolvedReference and the stage would be dropped — which is the failure this declaration exists to prevent. If the ordering in judge_spot_run.main ever changes so the plan key is read before the preflight return, the stage's preflight fails loudly against a plan that does not exist — the correct outcome, and not a silent pass.
